slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The essay states, citing a JMIR study, that a 2022 survey of 55 rural facilities found the majority using one or two digital tools, mainly DHIS2/eIDSR on tablets or mobiles for aggregate and weekly surveillance reporting; it also states that primary healthcare units fill paper forms HF1-HF9 for aggregate service reporting to NHMIS/DHIS2, without saying where those are keyed. The essay does not separate DHIS2 from eIDSR in the survey figure.
The essay states that rural primary healthcare units keep paper patient files at the point of care, and that a 2022 survey of 55 rural facilities (JMIR) found no EMR or patient registry in use.

The essay states, citing the Digital Health Roadmap 2024-2026, that EMR exists only as isolated pilots, naming a GOPA-GIZ pilot in 2 rural primary healthcare units in Kambia and Port Loko and planned QEHSSSP hub-and-spoke sites in selected rural districts, with no nationwide scaling; it gives no date, so the publication date is used.

systems.tiers: primary healthcare units (PHUs) report to it on paper forms HF1-HF9
1,500+ facilities nationwide by 2019, via mobile apps
2 rural PHUs in Kambia and Port Loko

note: Passages of an AI-assisted 54-country compilation; every figure is the essay's own summary of cited sources (JMIR 2022, WHO AFRO, the Roadmap), not a primary statement.
